Luxury Resorts

Best Luxury Family Resorts

By Priya Anand · May 15, 2026 · Updated August 29, 2026 · 8 min read

Luxury travel and family travel don’t automatically overlap — plenty of five-star resorts are built around adult-only quiet, not kids. The properties worth considering here have solved that specifically, with real family suites and kids’ programs that match the quality of everything else at the resort.

Quick facts

Typical nightly rate
$500+ per night
What sets luxury family resorts apart
Dedicated family suites and genuinely trained kids' club staff

Luxury and family-friendly aren't always the same thing

A lot of five-star resorts are excellent for a couple's trip and mediocre for a family one — because 'luxury' in hospitality has historically meant quiet, adult-focused spaces. The resorts on this list are the exceptions: properties that deliver a genuinely high-end experience without treating children as an inconvenience to manage around.

What to look for at this price point

Dedicated family suites or villas

Multi-room configurations with a separate space for kids, rather than a standard room with an extra bed wedged in — increasingly common at top-tier resorts but still worth confirming before booking.

Kids' clubs with real curriculum, not just supervision

The best luxury kids' clubs run structured, genuinely engaging programs — cooking classes, nature walks, cultural activities — rather than functioning as a screen-time babysitting service.

In-room childcare or babysitting services

A standard offering at this tier, and worth asking about availability and advance booking requirements if a parents-only dinner is part of the plan.

Age-appropriate spa and activity options

Some luxury resorts now offer scaled-down spa treatments or activity programs for tweens and teens, which can be a genuine trip highlight for that age group specifically.

Questions worth asking before booking

  • Is the kids' club included in the room rate, or an added daily fee?
  • What's the staff-to-child ratio, and is staff specifically trained in childcare or hospitality generally?
  • Are family suites or connecting rooms available, and how far ahead do they need to be booked?
  • Does the resort have a genuinely different atmosphere during school holiday weeks versus term time — worth knowing if quiet is part of what you're paying for

Getting the most from a luxury family stay

  • Book any specialty family suite configurations as early as possible — these are usually the first rooms to sell out
  • Use the kids' club deliberately for at least one adults-only dinner or spa visit — it's part of what you're paying for
  • Ask the concierge about family-specific excursions; luxury resorts often have better-curated options than generic tour bookings

Frequently asked questions

Are luxury resorts worth it for a family trip?

For families who want a higher standard of service and dedicated family accommodation, yes — but only at properties that have specifically invested in family infrastructure. Not every luxury resort has, so it's worth confirming before paying the premium.

What should you look for in a luxury resort's kids' club?

A real, structured activity schedule rather than open-ended supervision, trained staff, and enough capacity that your child isn't one of thirty kids with two staff members.

Do luxury resorts offer babysitting for date nights?

Most do, though availability can be limited during peak periods — it's worth booking any in-room childcare in advance rather than assuming it'll be available on request.
